Ablative of source/cause: from saṃbhava as an upāsanā, not a comparative ablative with anya.

Ablative of source/cause: from asaṃbhava/asambhūti as an upāsanā.

analysis.note: Marks the preceding statement as what has been heard.
Substantive masculine plural, ‘of/from the wise’; the bhāṣya supplies vacanam.
Relative pronoun referring to the dhīrāḥ.

Enclitic dative plural, ‘to us’; the same form can also serve as genitive. The linga value Pum is supplied only as the required formal subanta feature for this gender-neutral personal pronoun, not as a semantic masculine claim.
Accusative object of vicacakṣire; scoped by the bhāṣya as the result of worship of the manifest and unmanifest.
Ātmanepada perfect form; the bhāṣya glosses it with vyākhyātavanta, ‘they explained’.

justifications.decision: The neuter anyat is not left as an unspecified ‘something else’, nor is saṃbhavāt taken as the object of a simple comparative ‘other than saṃbhava’. Śaṅkara supplies phalam and glosses anyad eva with pṛthag eva, so the verse contrasts distinct results.
options_considered: ‘other than saṃbhava’ as a direct comparative
‘a distinct fruit/result from the relevant worship’
justifications.chosen: anyat eva = ‘quite/separately different is the fruit’

evidence.quote: anyadeva pṛthagevāhuḥ phalaṃ sambhavātsambhūteḥ kāryabrahmopāsanādaṇimādyaiśvaryalakṣaṇaṃ vyākhyātavanta ityarthaḥ
evidence.translation: ‘Different indeed’ means ‘separate indeed’; they explained the fruit from saṃbhava/sambhūti, from worship of the effect-Brahman, characterized by lordly powers beginning with aṇimā.
Those who explained that to us explained the fruit of worship of the manifest and the unmanifest.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara identifies saṃbhava with sambhūti and with kārya-brahmopāsanā. Thus the ablative denotes the source/cause, namely that upāsanā, not mere ‘birth’, ‘coming into being’, or an abstract metaphysical ‘existence’.
justifications.chosen: saṃbhavāt = ‘from saṃbhava/sambhūti, worship of the effect-Brahman’

evidence.translation: From saṃbhava, from sambhūti, from worship of the effect-Brahman, whose mark/result is lordly power beginning with aṇimā.
The fruit of worship of the manifest and the unmanifest.

justifications.decision: The commentary takes the second ablative as the counterpart of saṃbhava: asambhūti/avyākṛta-upāsanā. Line 2 is visibly unproofread around ‘asambhūtekhyākṛtād’; I do not rely on that corrupt-looking segment alone, but the following avyākṛtopāsanāt and line 3’s vyākṛtāvyākṛtopāsanaphalam fix the intended sense.
justifications.chosen: asaṃbhavāt = ‘from asaṃbhava/asambhūti, worship of the unmanifest’

evidence.translation: Likewise they said another [fruit] from asambhava/asambhūti … from worship of the unmanifest; the printed middle segment appears corrupt/unsegmented.
They explained the fruit of worship of the manifest and the unmanifest.

justifications.decision: The genitive dhīrāṇām is construed with an understood vacanam in the bhāṣya. Therefore the verse says that this teaching was received from the wise, not merely that ‘we heard wise men’.
options_considered: ‘we heard the wise men’ as a direct object
‘we heard the teaching of/from the wise’
justifications.chosen: śuśruma dhīrāṇām = ‘we have heard the teaching/from the wise’

evidence.translation: Thus we heard the speech/teaching of the wise. The printed dhīraṇāṃ is an unproofread spelling for dhīrāṇām.

justifications.decision: Although vi-√cakṣ can mean ‘see distinctly’, Śaṅkara glosses it as vyākhyātavanta, ‘they explained’. The object is tat, and naḥ is the recipient, ‘to us’. The scope of tat is the just-mentioned fruit of worship of the manifest and unmanifest.
options_considered: ‘who declared our that’ with naḥ as genitive
justifications.chosen: ye naḥ tad vicacakṣire = ‘who explained that to us’

evidence.translation: Those who explained that to us—i.e. explained the fruit of worship of the manifest and the unmanifest.

translation:
Quite different, they say, is the fruit from saṃbhava (sambhūti: worship of the effect-Brahman, kārya-brahman);
different, they say, is the fruit from asaṃbhava (asambhūti: worship of the unmanifest, avyākṛta).
Thus have we heard from the wise,
who explained that to us.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render saṃbhava/asaṃbhava as abstract ‘being/non-being’ or ‘birth/non-birth’; Śaṅkara instead reads them as two upāsanās: of the effect-Brahman/manifest and of the unmanifest.
It might miss the supplied phalam and translate ‘different from saṃbhava’ rather than ‘a different fruit from the worship called saṃbhava’.
It might take vicacakṣire in its visual sense ‘saw/perceived’; the bhāṣya explicitly glosses it as ‘explained’ (vyākhyātavanta).
It might take naḥ as genitive ‘our’; in context and in the commentary it is dative, ‘to us’.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 tagged naḥ as mad_PG, i.e. genitive plural; I take it as dative plural, ‘to us’, because tat is the object and the bhāṣya glosses ye nas tad vicacakṣire as ‘they explained that to us’ (line 3).
ByT5 gives vicakṣ as the verbal lemma; per the requested format I analyze this as bare root cakṣ with prefix vi.
open_questions: Commentary line 2 is unproofread around ‘asambhūtekhyākṛtād’; the translation relies on the clear avyākṛtopāsanāt in line 2 and vyākṛtāvyākṛtopāsanaphalam in line 3.
Commentary line 3 prints dhīraṇāṃ, evidently for dhīrāṇām; this does not affect the interpretation.
mula: anyad evāhuḥ saṃbhavād anyad āhur asaṃbhavāt | iti śuśruma dhīrāṇāṃ ye nas tad vicacakṣire
